content: LYK5, also referred to as STRADα, is a protein kinase encoded by the LYK5 gene in humans. Endogenously, LKB1 and STRADα form a functional complex in which STRADα activates LKB1. This activation leads to the phosphorylation of both LKB1 and STRADα. When endogenous LYK5 is depleted using small interfering RNA (siRNA), the ability of LKB1 to induce G1 phase cell cycle arrest is abolished. STRADα plays a critical role in stabilizing the LKB1 protein, both in living organisms (in vivo) and in controlled laboratory conditions (in vitro). Furthermore, when STRADα is overexpressed alongside LKB1 in cultured neurons derived from mouse embryonic cortices, it has the capacity to induce the formation of multiple axons. STRADα undergoes extensive splicing in vivo, and this splicing is regulated in a manner that is both developmentally timed and specific to certain tissues. However, the distinct biological roles of the various splice variants of STRADα remain unclear and require further investigation. Mutations in the LYK5/STRADα gene have been linked to a rare genetic disorder known as PMSE syndrome, which is characterized by polyhydramnios (excessive amniotic fluid during pregnancy), megalencephaly (abnormally large brain size), and symptomatic epilepsy. STRADα has been demonstrated to interact with two key proteins: LKB1 and MO25. These interactions are likely critical for its biological functions.
